big: You pay ₹30 for the right to buy a share at ₹500, no matter how high the market goes. If the market stays low, you walk away and lose only the ₹30. That is an option: a right, not a duty.

lines: So an option is like a booking fee?
Close. The premium is the price of the right. A call is the right to buy at a fixed strike price. A put is the right to sell. The buyer can lose no more than the premium, and it is not refunded.

intro: Made-up figures, for learning only. This is education, not a call to trade.
note: The strike price is the fixed price at which the holder can buy or sell if exercised.

title: Options basics
stops: A call is the right to buy at a fixed price
A put obliges the buyer to sell
The premium is the buyer's maximum loss
The premium is refunded if the option is unused
caps: It is a right, not a duty.

q: Which option gives the buyer the right to buy at a fixed price?
why: A put is the right to sell. It does not answer what was asked.
The premium is the price paid for the option.
A call is the right to buy at the strike price.
The strike is the fixed price, not the option type.

q: A buyer pays ₹30 per unit for an option. What is the most per unit the buyer can lose?
why: The premium paid is the maximum loss.
₹500 is a strike price, not the premium.
A buyer's loss is capped at the premium.
The premium is non-refundable, so loss can be ₹30.

q: An investor pays a fee for the right to sell a share at ₹400 even if the price falls lower. What is this?
why: A call is the right to buy. That does not match this case.
A future carries an obligation to trade. It does not fit the facts given.
A bonus issue gives holders extra shares. It does not answer what was asked.
A put is the right to sell at a fixed price. That matches the case described.

opts: The fee paid by the buyer up front
The fixed price to buy or sell at
The market price on the day today
The price on expiry day only
why: The fee paid is the premium. It does not fit the facts given.
It is fixed in the contract. This fits the facts given.
Market price moves; strike is fixed. The details here point elsewhere.
Strike is set at the start, not only at expiry. That does not match this case.

pts: An option is a right, not a duty, to buy (call) or sell (put) at a strike price.
The premium is the price of that right and the buyer's maximum loss.
The strike price is fixed in the contract.
